# About this script

**Primary, preregistered analysis (main text).** Full-time,
standard-daytime-shift participants.

Fits Models 1a, 1a + weekend, 1b, 2a, and 2b (raw TV; preregistered),
plus Model 2b with log1p TV (secondary; not preregistered). Run
`M2_data_structuring.Rmd` first. Fitted models, LOO, and k-fold objects
are cached in `model_fits_m2/fulltime_standard/`, so re-knitting reloads
them instead of refitting.

Robustness checks (not preregistered): 10-fold cross-validation for the
random-scale model comparisons, because many observations have Pareto
k > 0.7 even after moment matching; and Model 2b refit with `mi()` to
include days with sleep but missing TV.

Models with doubled iterations (bulk ESS < 1000 at 2000 iterations,
per the prereg): `model_2b_log`, `model_2b_mi`.

# Packages, data, and helper functions

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(brms)

M2_sample <- readRDS("M2_analysis_data_fulltime_standard.rds")

model_output_dir <- "model_fits_m2/fulltime_standard"
dir.create(model_output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

tag <- "fulltime_standard"

# Computes LOO once and caches it to disk
get_loo <- function(model, path) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    readRDS(path)
  } else {
    loo_result <- loo(model, moment_match = TRUE)
    saveRDS(loo_result, path)
    loo_result
  }
}

# kfold() runs refits through the future package, which by default
# refuses to pass objects over 500 MB (the fitted models are larger).
# Folds run one at a time in this session, so nothing is copied.
options(future.globals.maxSize = Inf)

# Computes 10-fold CV once and caches it to disk (refits are not saved,
# to keep disk use low)
get_kfold <- function(model, folds, path) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    readRDS(path)
  } else {
    kfold_result <- kfold(model, folds = folds, seed = 2026)
    saveRDS(kfold_result, path)
    kfold_result
  }
}

# Assigns K folds stratified by participant: each person's rows are
# shuffled and dealt across folds in turn, so their days land in different
# folds. Same algorithm as loo::kfold_split_stratified() in loo >= 2.9.0.
# Written out because loo 2.8.0 mishandles participants with a single row
# (sample(n) draws from 1:n), which silently un-stratifies the folds.
split_folds_by_id <- function(id, K = 10) {
  id <- as.integer(factor(id))
  row_order <- integer()
  for (person in seq_len(max(id))) {
    rows <- which(id == person)
    if (length(rows) > 1) rows <- sample(rows)
    row_order <- c(row_order, rows)
  }
  folds <- rep(NA_integer_, length(id))
  folds[row_order] <- rep(1:K, ceiling(length(id) / K))[seq_along(id)]
  folds
}

# Prereg convergence criteria: R-hat < 1.01, bulk and tail ESS > 1000,
# and 0 divergent transitions (population-level, SD, and correlation
# parameters; bsp_ and sigma_ cover the mi() model)
check_convergence <- function(fit) {
  draws_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(
    as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b_|bsp_|sd_|cor_|sigma$|sigma_)", regex = TRUE),
    "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
  )

  tibble(
    max_rhat = max(draws_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_bulk_ess = min(draws_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_tail_ess = min(draws_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    divergent = sum(nuts_params(fit, pars = "divergent__")$Value)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      meets_prereg = max_rhat < 1.01 & min_bulk_ess > 1000 &
        min_tail_ess > 1000 & divergent == 0
    )
}

# Prereg assumption check: Q-Q plot of level-1 residuals
check_residual_normality <- function(fit, label) {
  resid_est <- residuals(
    fit,
    method = "posterior_predict"
  )[, "Estimate"]

  qqnorm(
    resid_est,
    main = paste0(label, ": Level-1 residual Q-Q plot")
  )

  qqline(resid_est)
}
```

# Descriptive statistics

Sleep, TV, and weekend are summarized at the diary-day level; age and sex
at the participant level.

```{r}
# Outcome and TV predictors (diary-day level)
M2_sample %>%
  summarise(
    sleep_mean = mean(sleep_next_night_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    sleep_sd = sd(sleep_next_night_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    sleep_min = min(sleep_next_night_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    sleep_max = max(sleep_next_night_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    sleep_missing = sum(is.na(sleep_next_night_minutes)),

    tv_mean = mean(tv_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_sd = sd(tv_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_min = min(tv_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_max = max(tv_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_missing = sum(is.na(tv_duration_minutes)),

    tv_log_mean = mean(tv_duration_minutes_log, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_log_sd = sd(tv_duration_minutes_log, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_log_missing = sum(is.na(tv_duration_minutes_log))
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Weekend (diary-day level)
M2_sample %>%
  count(weekend)

# Age (participant level)
M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, age) %>%
  summarise(
    age_mean = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_sd = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_min = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_max = max(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_missing = sum(is.na(age))
  )

# Sex (participant level; 0 = male, 1 = female)
M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, sex) %>%
  count(sex)
```

```{r}
# Sleep and TV: overall M, SD, and median, plus between-person SD
# (SD of person means) and within-person SD (SD of deviations from
# each person's own mean)
describe_levels <- function(data, variable) {
  data %>%
    filter(!is.na({{ variable }})) %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    mutate(
      person_mean = mean({{ variable }}),
      deviation = {{ variable }} - person_mean
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean = mean({{ variable }}),
      sd = sd({{ variable }}),
      median = median({{ variable }}),
      between_person_sd = sd(person_mean[!duplicated(id)]),
      within_person_sd = sd(deviation)
    )
}

bind_rows(
  sleep_next_night_minutes = describe_levels(M2_sample, sleep_next_night_minutes),
  tv_duration_minutes = describe_levels(M2_sample, tv_duration_minutes),
  .id = "variable"
) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Complete TV-sleep pairs per participant (level-1 sample for Model 2b)
M2_sample %>%
  filter(!is.na(tv_duration_minutes), !is.na(sleep_next_night_minutes)) %>%
  count(id, name = "pairs") %>%
  summarise(
    total_pairs = sum(pairs),
    participants = n(),
    mean_pairs = mean(pairs),
    median_pairs = median(pairs),
    min_pairs = min(pairs),
    max_pairs = max(pairs)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

# Model 1a: unconditional means model

```{r}
message("Fitting model_1a (", tag, ")")
model_1a <- brm(
  sleep_next_night_minutes ~ 1 + (1 | id),
  data = M2_sample,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  file = file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("model_1a_", tag, "_m2")),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(model_1a, prob = 0.9)

# ICC
variance_components_1a <- VarCorr(model_1a)

between_person_var_1a <- variance_components_1a$id$sd[1, "Estimate"]^2
residual_var_1a <- variance_components_1a$residual__$sd[1, "Estimate"]^2
icc_1a <- between_person_var_1a /
  (between_person_var_1a + residual_var_1a)

fixef(model_1a, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))

between_person_var_1a
residual_var_1a
icc_1a
```

# Comparing Model 1a and the weekend-control model

The weekend indicator is retained in all later models regardless of this
comparison (prereg).

```{r}
loo_1a <- get_loo(model_1a, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("loo_1a_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
loo_weekend <- get_loo(model_weekend, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("loo_weekend_", tag, "_m2.rds")))

loo_compare(list(model_1a = loo_1a, model_weekend = loo_weekend))
```

# Model 1b: person-specific residual variance (random scale)

`sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)` lets the residual variance differ by person;
the shared `q` tag estimates the intercept-scale correlation.

```{r}
message("Fitting model_1b (", tag, ")")
model_1b <- brm(
  bf(
    sleep_next_night_minutes ~ 1 + weekend + (1 | q | id),
    sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)
  ),
  data = M2_sample,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  file = file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("model_1b_", tag, "_m2")),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(model_1b, prob = 0.9)
```

# Comparing the weekend-control model and Model 1b

The better-fitting residual structure is carried forward (prereg).

```{r}
loo_1b <- get_loo(model_1b, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("loo_1b_", tag, "_m2.rds")))

loo_compare(list(model_weekend = loo_weekend, model_1b = loo_1b))
```

# Model 2a: age and sex

Age is mean-centered at the participant level.

```{r}
age_mean <- M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, age) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(m)

M2_sample <- M2_sample %>%
  mutate(age_centered = age - age_mean)
```

```{r}
message("Fitting model_2a (", tag, ")")

model_2a <- brm(
  bf(
    sleep_next_night_minutes ~
      1 + weekend + age_centered + sex +
      (1 | q | id),

    sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)
  ),
  data = M2_sample,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  file = file.path(
    model_output_dir,
    paste0("model_2a_", tag, "_m2")
  ),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(model_2a, prob = 0.9)
```

# Model 2b: within- and between-person TV (raw minutes; preregistered)

TV is person-mean centered (`tv_within`), and each person's mean is
grand-mean centered across participants (`tv_person_mean`).

```{r}
M2_sample <- M2_sample %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    tv_person_mean_raw = mean(tv_duration_minutes, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_within = tv_duration_minutes - tv_person_mean_raw
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Equally weighted mean of participants' TV means
tv_grand_mean <- M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, tv_person_mean_raw) %>%
  summarise(
    grand_mean = mean(tv_person_mean_raw, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pull(grand_mean)

M2_sample <- M2_sample %>%
  mutate(
    tv_person_mean = tv_person_mean_raw - tv_grand_mean
  )

# QC: centered person means should average ~0
tv_grand_mean

M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, tv_person_mean_raw, tv_person_mean) %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n(),
    grand_mean_raw = mean(tv_person_mean_raw),
    grand_mean_centered = mean(tv_person_mean)
  )
```

```{r}
message("Fitting model_2b (", tag, ")")

model_2b <- brm(
  bf(
    sleep_next_night_minutes ~
      1 + weekend + age_centered + sex +
      tv_within + tv_person_mean +
      (1 | q | id),

    sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)
  ),
  data = M2_sample,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  file = file.path(
    model_output_dir,
    paste0("model_2b_", tag, "_m2")
  ),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(model_2b, prob = 0.9)
```

# Model 2b with log1p TV (secondary; not preregistered)

```{r}
M2_sample <- M2_sample %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(
    tv_log_person_mean_raw = mean(tv_duration_minutes_log, na.rm = TRUE),
    tv_log_within =
      tv_duration_minutes_log - tv_log_person_mean_raw
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

tv_log_grand_mean <- M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, tv_log_person_mean_raw) %>%
  summarise(
    grand_mean = mean(tv_log_person_mean_raw, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pull(grand_mean)

M2_sample <- M2_sample %>%
  mutate(
    tv_log_person_mean =
      tv_log_person_mean_raw - tv_log_grand_mean
  )

# QC: centered person means and within-person deviations should average ~0
M2_sample %>%
  distinct(id, tv_log_person_mean_raw, tv_log_person_mean) %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n(),
    grand_mean_raw = mean(tv_log_person_mean_raw, na.rm = TRUE),
    grand_mean_centered = mean(tv_log_person_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

M2_sample %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_tv_log_within = mean(tv_log_within, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    largest_absolute_mean =
      max(abs(mean_tv_log_within), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

```{r}
message("Fitting model_2b_log (", tag, ")")

model_2b_log <- brm(
  bf(
    sleep_next_night_minutes ~
      1 + weekend + age_centered + sex +
      tv_log_within + tv_log_person_mean +
      (1 | q | id),

    sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)
  ),
  data = M2_sample,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  # Iterations doubled per prereg (bulk ESS < 1000 at 2000 iterations)
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  file = file.path(
    model_output_dir,
    paste0("model_2b_log_", tag, "_m2")
  ),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(model_2b_log, prob = 0.9)
```

# Comparing Model 2a, Model 2b, and Model 2b (log)

`loo_compare()` needs every model fit to the same rows. Models 2b and
2b-log drop rows with missing TV, so Model 2a is refit on that
TV-complete subset only for these comparisons. The raw vs. log
comparison is not preregistered.

```{r}
M2_sample_tv_complete <- M2_sample %>%
  filter(!is.na(tv_duration_minutes))

message("Fitting model_2a_tv_complete (", tag, ")")

model_2a_tv_complete <- brm(
  bf(
    sleep_next_night_minutes ~
      1 + weekend + age_centered + sex +
      (1 | q | id),
    sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)
  ),
  data = M2_sample_tv_complete,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  warmup = 1000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  file = file.path(
    model_output_dir,
    paste0("model_2a_tv_complete_", tag, "_m2")
  ),
  file_refit = "never"
)

# QC: all compared models use the same observations
stopifnot(
  nobs(model_2a_tv_complete) == nobs(model_2b),
  nobs(model_2a_tv_complete) == nobs(model_2b_log)
)
```

```{r}
loo_2a_tv_complete <- get_loo(model_2a_tv_complete, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("loo_2a_tv_complete_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
loo_2b <- get_loo(model_2b, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("loo_2b_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
loo_2b_log <- get_loo(model_2b_log, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("loo_2b_log_", tag, "_m2.rds")))

# Pareto k diagnostics (after moment matching). All observations should
# be below 0.7 for the LOO estimates above to be reliable
loo_list <- list(
  model_1a = loo_1a,
  model_weekend = loo_weekend,
  model_1b = loo_1b,
  model_2a_tv_complete = loo_2a_tv_complete,
  model_2b = loo_2b,
  model_2b_log = loo_2b_log
)

for (model_name in names(loo_list)) {
  cat("\n", model_name, "\n")
  print(loo::pareto_k_table(loo_list[[model_name]]))
}

# Pareto k summary for reporting
bind_rows(lapply(loo_list, function(loo_result) {
  k <- loo::pareto_k_values(loo_result)
  tibble(
    n = length(k),
    n_k_above_0.7 = sum(k > 0.7),
    percent_k_above_0.7 = mean(k > 0.7) * 100,
    n_k_above_1 = sum(k > 1),
    max_k = max(k)
  )
}), .id = "model") %>%
  as.data.frame()

loo_compare(list(model_2a_tv_complete = loo_2a_tv_complete, model_2b = loo_2b))
loo_compare(list(model_2a_tv_complete = loo_2a_tv_complete, model_2b_log = loo_2b_log))
loo_compare(list(model_2b = loo_2b, model_2b_log = loo_2b_log))
```

# 10-fold cross-validation (robustness check; not preregistered)

LOO remains the preregistered comparison. Because many observations in
the random-scale models have Pareto k > 0.7 even after moment matching,
the same comparisons are repeated with 10-fold cross-validation. Folds
are stratified by participant, so each person's days are spread across
folds and held-out days are predicted for known participants (the same
target as LOO). Models in each comparison share one set of folds.
Model 1a vs. the weekend model is not repeated (no random scale; nearly
all Pareto k values are good).

```{r}
# Same rows, so the same folds apply to both models
stopifnot(nobs(model_weekend) == nobs(model_1b))

set.seed(2026)
folds_full <- split_folds_by_id(model_1b$data$id, K = 10)

set.seed(2026)
folds_tv <- split_folds_by_id(model_2b$data$id, K = 10)

# QC: every row has a fold, and no participant has two days in one fold
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(folds_full), !anyNA(folds_tv),
  !anyDuplicated(data.frame(model_1b$data$id, folds_full)),
  !anyDuplicated(data.frame(model_2b$data$id, folds_tv))
)

table(folds_full)
table(folds_tv)
```

```{r}
message("10-fold CV (", tag, ")")

kfold_weekend <- get_kfold(model_weekend, folds_full, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("kfold_weekend_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
kfold_1b <- get_kfold(model_1b, folds_full, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("kfold_1b_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
kfold_2a_tv_complete <- get_kfold(model_2a_tv_complete, folds_tv, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("kfold_2a_tv_complete_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
kfold_2b <- get_kfold(model_2b, folds_tv, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("kfold_2b_", tag, "_m2.rds")))
kfold_2b_log <- get_kfold(model_2b_log, folds_tv, file.path(model_output_dir, paste0("kfold_2b_log_", tag, "_m2.rds")))

loo_compare(list(model_weekend = kfold_weekend, model_1b = kfold_1b))
loo_compare(list(model_2a_tv_complete = kfold_2a_tv_complete, model_2b = kfold_2b))
loo_compare(list(model_2a_tv_complete = kfold_2a_tv_complete, model_2b_log = kfold_2b_log))
loo_compare(list(model_2b = kfold_2b, model_2b_log = kfold_2b_log))
```

# Model 2b with missing TV imputed (sensitivity; not preregistered)

Model 2b drops days with sleep but no TV report. Here those days are
kept, and `tv_within` on those days is imputed with `mi()`, jointly with
the sleep model. TV person means are from each participant's observed
TV days, as in Model 2b. The imputation model is Gaussian, so imputed
TV values can be negative.

```{r}
M2_sample_sleep_complete <- M2_sample %>%
  filter(!is.na(sleep_next_night_minutes))

# QC: days with sleep but missing TV (imputed), and no missing person means
M2_sample_sleep_complete %>%
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    missing_tv_within = sum(is.na(tv_within)),
    missing_tv_person_mean = sum(is.na(tv_person_mean))
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
message("Fitting model_2b_mi (", tag, ")")

model_2b_mi <- brm(
  bf(
    sleep_next_night_minutes ~
      1 + weekend + age_centered + sex +
      mi(tv_within) + tv_person_mean +
      (1 | q | id),

    sigma ~ 1 + (1 | q | id)
  ) +
    bf(tv_within | mi() ~ 1 + weekend) +
    set_rescor(FALSE),
  data = M2_sample_sleep_complete,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  # Iterations doubled per prereg (bulk ESS < 1000 at 2000 iterations)
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  seed = 2026,
  file = file.path(
    model_output_dir,
    paste0("model_2b_mi_", tag, "_m2")
  ),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(model_2b_mi, prob = 0.9)

# Observations used (Model 2b vs. imputed model)
c(model_2b = nobs(model_2b), model_2b_mi = nrow(model_2b_mi$data))

# TV coefficients, Model 2b vs. imputed model
tv_effects <- function(fit) {
  estimates <- fixef(fit, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))
  rows <- grep("tv_within$|tv_person_mean$", rownames(estimates))
  tibble(
    term = sub(".*(tv_within|tv_person_mean)$", "\\1", rownames(estimates)[rows]),
    as_tibble(estimates[rows, , drop = FALSE])
  )
}

bind_rows(
  model_2b = tv_effects(model_2b),
  model_2b_mi = tv_effects(model_2b_mi),
  .id = "model"
) %>%
  arrange(term, model) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Convergence (prereg criteria; should show meets_prereg = TRUE)
check_convergence(model_2b_mi) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

# Model diagnostics (prereg convergence and residual checks)

```{r}
models <- list(
  model_1a = model_1a,
  model_weekend = model_weekend,
  model_1b = model_1b,
  model_2a = model_2a,
  model_2a_tv_complete = model_2a_tv_complete,
  model_2b = model_2b,
  model_2b_log = model_2b_log
)

# Observations used by each model
sapply(models, nobs)

# Convergence: every row should show meets_prereg = TRUE
bind_rows(lapply(models, check_convergence), .id = "model") %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
# Level-1 residual normality
for (model_name in names(models)) {
  check_residual_normality(models[[model_name]], model_name)
}
```
